title: arxiv_2303.03366v2
universal_lens: Cross-modal fusion in RMOT unifies visual and linguistic embeddings via attention mechanisms, enabling dynamic referent object prediction through temporal consistency. A unified framework for spatio-temporal grounding of natural language in video using bidirectional transformer encoders and cross-modal attention mechanisms.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference maps linguistic queries to probabilistic object hypotheses using conformal predictive distributions over visual features and temporal contexts. Bayesian inference over latent spatio-temporal regions conditioned on linguistic embeddings via conformal prediction intervals for uncertainty quantification.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning encodes multi-object referents as state transitions in a spatiotemporal graph, where each node represents an object's trajectory under referential constraints. Situation-aware state transitions driven by referential grounding operators that map sentence tokens to video object trajectories through dynamic attention kernels.

reasoning_traces.think: The core challenge in RMOT is bridging the gap between discrete linguistic descriptions and continuous object trajectories. We formalize this as a set-to-set mapping problem, where the goal is to predict a variable-sized set of object bounding boxes conditioned on a natural language query. This requires a differentiable loss function that handles set cardinality mismatches. Our proposed method leverages a bipartite matching cost combined with Hungarian assignment to ensure one-to-one correspondence between predicted boxes and ground-truth references. The training objective minimizes the weighted sum of classification and localization errors while respecting the dynamic nature of object appearances and disappearances. Empirically, we observe that the model excels in scenarios with clear spatial separation but struggles when objects share similar visual features or undergo occlusions. Future work should explore incorporating graph neural networks to explicitly model pairwise object interactions. reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 3 focuses on the formulation and evaluation of Referring Multi-Object Tracking (RMOT), extending traditional referring comprehension to handle multiple targets simultaneously. The core innovation lies in integrating cross-modal fusion with temporal tracking to enable robust referent identification. The method employs a Transformer-based architecture that processes both visual inputs and natural language queries concurrently. A key contribution is the introduction of a referential threshold βref=0.4 to filter true object candidates from visible ones. This approach addresses limitations of prior single-object models by allowing flexible multi-target interpretation. Evaluation on Refer-KITTI demonstrates superior performance over CNN-based competitors and even some Transformer variants. The framework supports generalization beyond training data through its modular design, enabling recognition of complex expressions like 'the left persons in black'. Temporal consistency ensures stable tracking across frames, while cross-modal alignment allows precise mapping between linguistic intent and visual reality. The results suggest that combining strong language understanding with dynamic visual tracking creates a powerful foundation for real-world applications requiring contextual object selection. Mathematical formalization involves defining operators that transform discrete linguistic tokens into continuous spatio-temporal regions, enabling precise localization tasks.
